findings.reason: a node following the assertion sentence would keep `north_stars` in `DERIVED_STATE_KEYS` and assert a value no code path fills, contradicting the deliverable it is implementing; this is the residual half of the earlier review's north-stars finding, whose fix removed the key from the literal list but not from the assertion sentence.
findings.text: §10's first case still asserts the kept set as "every block `derivedBlocks` returns, together with the milestones and north stars", but the same bullet's literal key set and §10's deliverable (line 235, "North stars are outside this section: on the index path the merge never fills them, so there is nothing to keep") both exclude north stars, so the case as written cannot be satisfied: `mergeDerived` (`state-loader.js:503-519`) assigns no `north_stars`, and `derivedBlocks` (`state-loader.js:334-351`) returns no such key

findings.reason: the node cannot show the gate can go red without a corpus large enough for the cold build to exceed 1 s, and §3's own gate set the precedent by naming 200 documents; one clause naming the control's scale closes it.
findings.text: §7's `/_index` clause control ("the persisted metadata index is removed before the restart, and the first pass's `/_index` gate fails") is run "against a temporary `reckon serve`" whose project scale is unstated, while the cost that can make it fail is the cold build's parse of every document: the endpoint builds lazily per request (`serve.py:3246` → `_served_index_rows`, `serve.py:1159-1175` → `metadata_index.index_rows`), so on a temporary mount of a handful of documents the first `/_index` answers well inside the 1 s bound even with the index removed, the control passes, and the section's only gate clause is left with no demonstrated falsifier
